SUM(f.FREE), :"SYS_B_10")) / SUM(df.BYTES) * :"SYS_B_11" END, :"SYS_B_12") AS USED_FILE_PCT, ROUND(CASE SUM(df.MAX_BYTES) WHEN :"SYS_B_13" THEN :"SYS_B_14 " ELSE NVL(SUM(df.BYTES) - SUM(f.FREE), :"SYS_B_15") / SUM(df.MAX_BYTES) * :"SYS_B_16" END, :"SYS_B_17") AS USED_FROM_MAX_PCT, CASE df.STATUS WHEN :"SYS_B_18" THEN :"SYS_B_19" WHEN :"SYS_B_20" THEN :"SYS_B_21" WHEN :"SYS_B_22" THEN :"SYS_B_23" ELSE :"SYS_B_24" END AS STATUS FROM (SELECT ct.CON$NAME AS CON_NAME, cdf.FILE_ID, ct.CONTENTS, ct.STATUS, cdf.FILE_NAME, cdf.TABLESPACE_NAME, TRUNC(cdf.BYTES) AS BYTES, TRUNC(GREATEST(cdf.BYTES, cdf.MAXBYTES)) AS MAX_BYTES FROM CDB_DATA_FILES cdf, CDB_TABLESPACES ct WHERE cdf.TABLESPACE_NAME = ct.TABLESPACE_NAME AND cdf.CON_ID = ct.CON_ID AND (ct.CON_ID = :"SYS_B_25" or (ct.CON$NAME is null and ct.CON_ID = :"SYS_B_26")) AND cdf.TABLESPACE_NAME = :"SYS_B_27" AND ct.CONTENTS = :"SYS_B_28") df, (SELECT TRUNC(SUM(BYTES)) AS FREE, FILE_ID FROM CDB_FREE_SPACE GROUP BY FILE_ID) f WHERE df.FILE_ID = f.FILE_ID (+) GROUP BY df.CON_NAME, df.TABLESPACE_NAME, df.CONTENTS, df.STATUS UNION ALL SELECT Y.CON_NAME, Y.NAME AS TABLESPACE, Y.CONTENTS AS TYPE, NVL(SUM(Y.BYTES), :"SYS_B_29") AS FILE_BYTES, NVL(SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES), :"SYS_B_30") AS MAX_BYTES, NVL(MAX(NVL(Y.FREE_BYTES, :"SYS_B_31")), :"SYS_B_32") AS FREE_BYTES, NVL(SUM(Y.BYTES) - MAX(Y.FREE_BYTES), :"SYS_B_33") AS USED_BYTES, ROUND(CASE SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES) WHEN :"SYS_B_34" THEN :"SYS_B_35" ELSE (SUM(Y.BYTES) / SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES) * :"SYS_B_36") END, :"SYS_B_37") AS USED_PCT_MAX, ROUND(CASE SUM(Y.BYTES) WHEN :"SYS_B_38" THEN :"SYS_B_39" ELSE (NVL(SUM(Y.BYTES) - MAX(Y.FREE_BYTES), :"SYS_B_40")) / SUM(Y.BYTES) * :"SYS_B_41" END, :"SYS_B_42") AS USED_FILE_PCT, ROUND(CASE SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES) WHEN :"SYS_B_43" THEN :"SYS_B_44" ELSE (NVL(SUM(Y.BYTES) - MAX(Y.FREE_BYTES), :"SYS_B_45")) / SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES) * :"SYS_B_46" END, :"SYS_B_47") AS USED_FROM_MAX_PCT, CASE Y.STATUS WHEN :"SYS_B_48" THEN :"SYS_B_49" WHEN :"SYS_B_50" THEN :"SYS_B_51" WHEN :"SYS_B_52" THEN :"SYS_B_53" ELSE :"SYS_B_54" END AS STATUS FROM (SELECT ct.CON$NAME AS CON_NAME, ctf.TABLESPACE_NAME AS NAME, ct.CONTENTS, ctf.STATUS AS STATUS, ctf.BYTES AS BYTES, (SELECT ((f.TOTAL_BLOCKS - s.TOT_USED_BLOCKS) * vp.VALUE) FROM (SELECT CON_ID, TABLESPACE_NAME, SUM(USED_BLOCKS) TOT_USED_BLOCKS FROM V$SORT_SEGMENT WHERE TABLESPACE_NAME != :"SYS_B_55" GROUP BY CON_ID, TABLESPACE_NAME) s, (SELECT CON_ID, TABLESPACE_NAME, SUM(BLOCKS) TOTAL_BLOCKS FROM CDB_TEMP_FILES WHERE TABLESPACE_NAME != :"SYS_B_56" GROUP BY CON_ID, TABLESPACE_NAME) f, (SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = :"SYS_B_57") vp WHERE f.TABLESPACE_NAME = s.TABLESPACE_NAME AND f.TABLESPACE_NAME = ctf.TABLESPACE_NAME AND f.CON_ID = s.CON_ID AND f.CON_ID = ct.CON_ID) AS FREE_BYTES, CASE WHEN ctf.MAXBYTES = :"SYS_B_58" THEN ctf.BYTES ELSE ctf.MAXBYTES END AS MAX_BYTES FROM CDB_TEMP_FILES ctf, CDB_TABLESPACES ct WHERE ctf.TABLESPACE_NAME = ct.TABLESPACE_NAME AND ctf.CON_ID = ct.CON_ID AND (ct.CON_ID = :"SYS_B_59" or (ct.CON$NAME is null and ct.CON_ID = :"SYS_B_60")) AND ctf.TABLESPACE_NAME = :"SYS_B_61" AND ct.CONTENTS = :"SYS_B_62") Y GROUP BY Y.CON_NAME, Y.NAME, Y.CONTENTS, Y.STATUS

ADDM Task ADDM:659179364_1_16501

          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:659179364_1_16501'
          ---------------------------------------------

Analysis Period
---------------
AWR snapshot range from 16500 to 16501.
Time period starts at 09-MAR-26 11.30.42 AM
Time period ends at 09-MAR-26 12.30.07 PM

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'KRISHNA' with DB ID 659179364.
Database version during analysis period was 19.29.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance krishna, numbered 1 and hosted at
kirshnadb-pr.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 32941 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 9.24.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                         Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                       Percent of Activity
   ----------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect      1.87 | 20.26         1
2  Soft Parse                          1.73 | 18.71         2
3  Undersized SGA                      .6 | 6.55            1
4  Hard Parse Due to Invalidations     .55 | 5.99           1
5  Top SQL Statements                  .36 | 3.93           1
6  Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria  .25 | 2.67           1
7  Commits and Rollbacks               .23 | 2.45           1


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.87 active sessions, 20.26% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.87 active sessions, 20.26% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.73 active sessions, 18.71% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.73 active sessions, 18.71% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.73 active sessions, 18.71% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "200" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Undersized SGA
Impact is .6 active sessions, 6.55% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "184320 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .52 active sessions, 5.65% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      264960 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.18 active sessions, 12.75% of total activity.
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .19 active sessions, 2.01% of total activity.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .55 active sessions, 5.99% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .55 active sessions, 5.99% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.18 active sessions, 12.75% of total activity.


Finding 5: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .36 active sessions, 3.93% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .36 active sessions, 3.93% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 4% for SQL execution,
      48% for parsing, 48% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.


Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .25 active sessions, 2.67% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .25 active sessions, 2.67% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.18 active sessions, 12.75% of total activity.


Finding 7: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .23 active sessions, 2.45% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .23 active sessions, 2.45% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 12 K and the
      average time per write was 0 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 5.7 M per second for
      reads and 7.8 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 57% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 42% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .23 active sessions, 2.45% of total activity.
